label: Causal coverage of sampled cessation
definition: CessationHasCause m means: for every numerical bearer x and natural-number sample n, if x exists at n and not at n+1, some existing ProtectiveProcess process has an occurring terminal transition from n to n+1 directed to that same x. This is the cessation instance of a causal requirement, an explicit OPEN hypothesis about supplied dictionaries, not a definition of real causation.
note: The existing Model primitives carry occurs, terminal, threat source/target and existsAt. DestructionSound separately restores that terminal occurrences really lose the same previously present bearer in the controls. NoCessationCause excludes all such terminal occurrences for x on the step. ContinuedGiving requires SOME giver at n+1 only when the same received bearer is present both before and after; the giver need not be original or distinct. UngivenContinuationFails says that a prior-present received bearer cannot persist to the next sample without any giver: its classical equivalence with ContinuedGiving is a warrant diagnostic, not independent support for either. ConsumerRestriction applies existing ConcurrentlyActualized to these same bearer/time inputs after explicit selected-world presence correspondence. Original Giving and received-esse meanings remain primitive and open; no withdrawal process is identified by definition. Controls reuse the exact inertia and sustained histories; one terminal process represents the loss of true in inertia at sample2 while recipient false persists without later giving. They certify structural assignments only, not metaphysical possibility or a real case of unsustained received esse. Sampled local loss coverage is weaker in scope than a law for all changes; it does not address the first sample, births or dense-time limits. No transitivity, causal well-foundedness, new production at each instant, counterfactual definition of causation or original-cause concurrence is inferred. Root purpose and applicability/reopening conditions are recorded in docs/eternity-dependence-connection.md.
